name: PCM1754DBQR
title: 24-bit, 192 kHz stereo delta-sigma audio DAC (PCM1753, PCM1754, PCM1755)
summary: A family of stereo 24-bit audio DACs built on an eight-level, fourth-order delta-sigma modulator, sampling from 5 kHz to 200 kHz on one 5 V supply in a 16-pin SSOP. Each output gives 4 VPP typical around 0.5 VCC with 106 dB dynamic range and SNR. The PCM1754 is set by pins (I2S or 16-bit right-justified, soft mute, 44.1 kHz de-emphasis, one zero flag); the PCM1753 and PCM1755 add a three-wire register port with attenuation, more formats and filter choices.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 5.5 V, 16 mA typ at 44.1 kHz

circuits.title: Basic connection
circuits.description: The PCM1754 in hardware mode on a single +5 V rail. The serial audio port (BCK, DATA, LRCK) and the system clock come in from the digital source; FMT, MUTE and DEMP are logic levels set from outside, and ZEROA leaves as a zero-data flag that can drive a mute. TEST, DGND and AGND go to ground and NC is left open. C1 is the 10 µF bulk capacitor on VCC and C4 the 10 µF on VCOM. Each analog output passes through its own 10 µF coupling capacitor (C2, C3), positive side at the chip, on its way to an outside low-pass post filter.
notes: Series resistors of 22 Ω to 100 Ω in the SCK, LRCK, BCK and DATA lines are recommended; with board and pin capacitance they form a low-pass that cuts emissions and damps ringing.

circuits.title: Single-supply output filter biased from VCOM
circuits.description: One channel's output filter on the 5 V supply alone. Half an OPA2353 forms a second-order multiple-feedback low-pass: R1 from VOUTX to the junction node, C2 from there to ground, R2 back from the op-amp output, R3 on to the inverting input and C1 from the inverting input to the output. The non-inverting input sits at VCOM, which C3 (10 µF) decouples, so the stage works around 0.5 VCC. Gain is -R2/R1, set to -1. A 10 µF capacitor (C4) takes the dc bias off the filtered output. X stands for L or R.

parts.note: equal to R1 for a gain of -1

notes: U1's VOUTL stands for either output; the right channel is the same circuit on VOUTR.
Op-amp pins: 1 output, 2 inverting input, 3 non-inverting input.

circuits.title: VCOM buffered by a voltage follower
circuits.description: When VCOM has to bias several nodes, an OPA337 wired as a unity-gain follower drives them instead of the unbuffered pin. VCOM keeps its 10 µF decoupling capacitor (C1) and feeds the follower's non-inverting input; the output, tied back to the inverting input, is the buffered VCOM.

circuits.title: Dual-supply output filter
circuits.description: A second-order Butterworth low-pass in the multiple-feedback form for a split-supply design, built on an OPA2134. VIN, the DAC output, goes through R1 to a node with C2 to ground and R2 back from the op-amp output; R3 continues to the inverting input, which C1 ties to the output. The non-inverting input is grounded. R4 sits in series with the output to VOUT. Gain is -R2/R1.
notes: The op-amp supply connections are not given. Op-amp pins: 1 output, 2 inverting input, 3 non-inverting input.

operation.text: A stereo audio DAC: the serial input feeds a 4x/8x oversampling digital filter and then a delta-sigma modulator with an eight-level quantizer and fourth-order noise shaping, followed per channel by a DAC, an output amplifier and a continuous-time RC low-pass. The combined oversampling of filter and modulator is 64 fS. A multilevel quantizer is steadier and less sensitive to clock jitter than a two-level one.

PCM1753 and PCM1755 are programmed through a three-wire control port (ML, MC, MD) and accept right-justified (16, 18, 20, 24 bit), I2S and left-justified data. PCM1754 has no control port: FMT, MUTE and DEMP pins choose I2S (16 to 24 bit) or 16-bit right-justified data, soft mute and 44.1 kHz de-emphasis, and it has one common zero flag. PCM1755 is rated -25 °C to 85 °C and its zero flags are open drain; the others are rated -40 °C to 85 °C. PCM1753 matches the PCM1748, PCM1742 and PCM1741 pinout apart from pin 5.

SCK (pin 16) runs the interpolation filter and modulator. Rates of 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768 or 1152 fS are detected automatically. The cleaner the clock (low phase jitter, low noise), the better the results; the PLL170x clock generators are suggested as a source.

With SCK running, reset starts once VCC passes about 3 V (2.2 V to 3.7 V) and lasts 1024 system clocks, during which the outputs sit at bipolar zero, VCC/2. A register is then initialized within the next 1/fS, and with SCK, BCK and LRCK present the outputs follow the data with unit group delay.

BCK, DATA and LRCK form a three-wire synchronous input; data is clocked in on BCK rising edges and LRCK runs at fS. Both clocks should be synchronous to SCK, ideally divided from it. In right-justified format BCK can be 32, 48 or 64 fS, with 32 fS only for 16-bit data; in I2S and left-justified it is 48 or 64 fS, and 48 fS only with a 192, 384 or 768 fS system clock. A change of LRCK rate, or SCK or BCK stopping for 3 bit clocks or more, halts the internal operation; once the clocks return it resynchronizes by itself within 3/fS, with no external reset. All formats take MSB-first two's-complement data; in standard and left-justified formats LRCK is high for the left channel, in I2S it is low. The default format of the programmable parts is 24-bit left-justified.

On the PCM1754, ZEROA goes to logic 1 when both channels' data has stayed at zero for 1024 sample periods. On the PCM1753 and PCM1755 each channel is detected separately and drives ZEROL (pin 12) or ZEROR (pin 11); register 22 can invert their polarity (ZREV) or combine them into one common flag on pin 11 (AZRO). The flags can drive an external mute or report to a controller.

VOUTL and VOUTR are single-ended outputs biased at 0.5 VCC, each able to swing 4 VPP (typical) across a 5 kΩ load coupled through a capacitor. The on-chip RC filter alone does not remove enough of the shaped out-of-band noise for many uses, so an external low-pass after the DAC is needed.
Pin 10 brings out the unbuffered mid-supply voltage, nominally 0.5 VCC, for a decoupling capacitor. It can bias an outside stage directly, or through a voltage follower when several nodes need it.
The PCM1754 sets its modulator to 64x oversampling at every system clock rate and sampling frequency.

The control port runs independently of the audio port. Each write is a 16-bit word on MD, MSB first: a 0, a seven-bit register index IDX[6:0], then eight data bits D[7:0]. ML is held high between writes; it is pulled low, 16 MC clocks shift the word in, and ML is raised again to latch it into the addressed register.

Each channel has its own digital attenuator, 0 dB to -63 dB in 0.5 dB steps, plus mute. A new setting is reached one 0.5 dB step every 8/fS. Setting MUTx ramps that channel down to mute at the same rate, without a pop; clearing it ramps back up to the stored level.

OVER doubles the oversampling rate, and OVER = 1 is advised at 192 kHz sampling (128 or 192 fS system clock). SRST performs the same initialization as power-on reset, clearing every register. DACx = 1 holds that output at bipolar zero, 0.5 VCC. DM12 turns on de-emphasis and DMF[1:0] picks its rate (44.1, 48 or 32 kHz). FLT picks sharp or slow filter rolloff. DREV inverts the output phase.

Noise shaping pushes quantization noise above fS/2, and it must be filtered out after the DAC by the on-chip filter together with an external active low-pass. The recommended filters are second-order Butterworth multiple-feedback stages, a topology with low sensitivity to part tolerance and temperature; the OPA2353 (single supply) and OPA2134 (dual supply) are the suggested op amps. The analog circuit after the DAC sets much of the system's performance.

VCC is 5 V (4.5 V to 5.5 V). The 10 µF capacitors of the basic connection are tantalum or aluminum electrolytic. Separate analog and digital supplies are preferred so digital switching noise stays off the analog rail; where one 5 V supply feeds both, an RF choke or ferrite bead goes between the digital and analog 5 V connections.

For THD+N the test signal is a 1 kHz digital sine at full scale, 24-bit, sampled at 44.1 kHz or 96 kHz, through the DAC post filter, with the analyzer band-limited (400 Hz high-pass, 30 kHz low-pass, AES17 filter at 20.9 kHz). Dynamic range uses the same chain with a -60 dB input and A-weighting; SNR uses all-zero data with the generator's dither off. Without A-weighting results are about 3 dB worse. The post filter on the evaluation board has its -3 dB point at 54 kHz or 108 kHz.

Use a ground plane split or cut between the analog and digital sections, and turn the chip so its digital I/O pins face the split, keeping the audio and control lines from the digital side short. The chip itself sits in the analog section, with the output circuits. In the single-supply plan the sections share a common ground and an RF choke or ferrite bead feeds the digital VDD from the +5 V analog supply.
